amphicoelias:eswiki:5.title: Amphicoelias altus (La guerra de los huesos)

facts.statement: The genus Amphicoelias was described by Edward Drinker Cope in 1878.
facts.quote: parent_authority: Cope, 1878

facts.statement: Amphicoelias was moderately sized, reaching about 18 meters in length and 15 metric tons in body mass, which is shorter than its relative Diplodocus.
facts.quote: Amphicoelias was moderately sized at about 18 m in length and 15 MT in body mass, shorter than its close relative Diplodocus.

facts.statement: Amphicoelias had very long and thin hindlimbs and forelimbs that were proportionally longer than in its relatives.
facts.quote: Its hindlimbs were very long and thin, and its forelimbs were proportionally longer than in relatives.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Amphicoelias altus, cataloged as AMNH 5764, contains uncertain material regarding which bones belong to the species.
facts.quote: The namesake fossil of the type species Amphicoelias altus, American Museum of Natural History (AMNH) 5764, is uncertain in included material.

facts.statement: Additional material found near the holotype, which was not mentioned by Cope, was similar to Diplodocus and later reidentified as such by Osborn and Mook.
facts.quote: The additional material, not mentioned by Cope, was found close in proximity to the holotype and was similar to Diplodocus, a relative of Amphicoelias.

facts.statement: In 1877, Cope named the species Amphicoelias latus based on a femur and tail vertebrae.
facts.quote: During the description of Amphicoelias altus in 1877, Cope additionally named A. latus, for a femur and tail vertebrae.

facts.statement: In 1878, Cope named Amphicoelias fragillimus based on a gigantic dorsal vertebra that was later lost.
facts.quote: A year later 1878, Cope named the third species of Amphicoelias, A. fragillimus for a gigantic dorsal vertebra that was subsequently lost.

facts.statement: Early estimates suggested Amphicoelias fragillimus could have been between 40 and 60 meters long, based on a 2.7-meter dorsal vertebra.
facts.quote: Measuring approximately 2.7 m if reconstructed based on Diplodocus, early estimates for the length of the animal in life were between 40 and 60 m long.

facts.statement: In 2018, Kenneth Carpenter renamed Amphicoelias fragillimus as the genus Maraapunisaurus and reclassified it from Diplodocidae to Rebbachisauridae.
facts.quote: In 2018, Kenneth Carpenter renamed Amphicoelias fragillimus as the new genus Maraapunisaurus, and reclassified it from Diplodocidae to Rebbachisauridae.

facts.statement: Fossils were discovered in 1877 by Oramel William Lucas in rock outcrops near Cañon City, Colorado.
facts.quote: In 1877, a number of fossils were discovered by Oramel William Lucas in rock outcrops in Colorado close to Cañon City.

facts.statement: The fossils were sent to Edward Drinker Cope on October 21, 1877.
facts.quote: They were sent to Cope on October 21, 1877.

facts.statement: Cope named the new sauropod taxon Amphicoelias altus in December 1877.
facts.quote: Cope concluded they belonged to a new taxon within Sauropoda, which Cope named Amphicoelias altus in December 1877.

facts.statement: Cope sold his fossil collection to the American Museum of Natural History in 1895.
facts.quote: Cope sold his collection of fossils to the American Museum of Natural History (AMNH) in 1895.

facts.statement: Collection data determined the specimen came from the youngest layers of the Late Jurassic Morrison Formation, separate from the layers containing Camarasaurus fossils.
facts.quote: Based on collection data, the specimen was determined to have come from the Late Jurassic-era Morrison Formation, in the youngest layers, separate from those that held the Camarasaurus fossils also described by Cope.

facts.statement: Amphicoelias possessed amphicoelous vertebrae, meaning both ends of the centrum were mildly to moderately concave.
facts.quote: Instead, Amphicoelias had amphicoelous vertebrae, where both ends are mildly to moderately concave.

facts.statement: Both Amphicoelias and Camarasaurus had accessory articulations in the neural arch, termed hyposphene by Cope, which limited the motion of vertebrae relative to one another.
facts.quote: However, both families also had accessory articulations in the neural arch, which Cope termed the hyposphene, limiting the motion of vertebrae respective to one another.

facts.statement: In 1881, Othniel Charles Marsh found Amphicoeliidae and Amphicoelias to be intermediate and poorly defined, noting that the primary feature of mildly concave articular faces was widespread in sauropods like Brontosaurus excelsus.
facts.quote: Amphicoeliidae and Amphicoelias were both found to be intermediate and poorly defined by paleontologist Othniel Charles Marsh in 1881, wherein the primary feature-two mildly concave articular faces-was shown to be widespread and also found in sauropods like Brontosaurus excelsus.

facts.statement: The femur of Amphicoelias latus measures 1.4 meters in length, though its proximal end is incomplete.
facts.quote: The femur is 1.4 m long, but the very proximal end is not fully preserved.

facts.statement: Amphicoelias fragillimus was originally known only from a single incomplete neural arch that stood 1.5 meters tall.
facts.quote: The third named Amphicoelias species, A. fragillimus, was known only from a single, incomplete 1.5 m tall neural arch, either last or second to last in the series of back vertebrae.

facts.statement: Based on an 1878 illustration, the single vertebra of A. fragillimus was estimated to be 2.7 meters tall in life.
facts.quote: Based only on an illustration published in 1878, this vertebra would have measured 2.7 m tall in life.

facts.statement: Some researchers argue that a typographical error in the original scale bar means the vertebra of A. fragillimus was actually only 1.38 meters tall.
facts.quote: However, it has been argued that the scale bar in the published description contained a typographical error, and the fossil vertebra was in fact only 1.38 m tall.

facts.statement: In 2018, A. fragillimus was reclassified into its own genus, Maraapunisaurus, and identified as a primitive rebbachisaurid.
facts.quote: In 2018, A. fragillimus was given its own genus, Maraapunisaurus, and reclassified as a primitive rebbachisaurid.

facts.statement: The femur of Amphicoelias is characterized by being unusually long, slender, and round in cross-section.
facts.quote: The femur of Amphicoelias is unusually long, slender, and round in cross section

facts.statement: The holotype of Amphicoelias includes a single slender right femur that is 1.524 meters long.
facts.quote: A single, slender right femur of Amphicoelias is known from the holotype, 1.524 m long.

facts.statement: A partial forelimb provisionally assigned to Amphicoelias resembles Diplodocus but is more robust overall.
facts.quote: A partial forelimb, provisionally referred to Amphicoelias by Osborn & Mook in 1921, resembles Diplodocus but is more robust overall.

facts.statement: The preserved scapula of Amphicoelias is 161 cm long and is thicker than that of Diplodocus but thinner than that of Camarasaurus.
facts.quote: 161 cm long as preserved, the bone is noticeably thicker than in Diplodocus, but not quite as thick as in Camarasaurus.

facts.statement: The ulna of Amphicoelias is more elongate than any comparable ulna known from Diplodocus.
facts.quote: The ulna is more elongate than any comparable bone known from Diplocodus.

facts.statement: In 2007, John Foster suggested that differences between A. altus and Diplodocus are not significant and may result from individual variation.
facts.quote: In 2007, John Foster suggested that the differences usually cited to differentiate Amphicoelias altus from the more well known Diplodocus are not significant and may be due to individual variation.

facts.statement: Emanuel Tschopp and colleagues disputed the synonymy of Amphicoelias and Diplodocus in a 2015 phylogenetic analysis.
facts.quote: This conclusion was disputed by Emanuel Tschopp et al. in 2015, where Amphicoelias was analysed as part of an extensive specimen-level phylogenetic analysis of Diplodocidae.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analyses have supported two placements for Amphicoelias: as the basalmost genus within Apatosaurinae or nested between B. excelsus and B. yahnahpin.
facts.quote: There were two strongly supported placements found for Amphicoelias, as the basalmost genus within Apatosaurinae, and as an apatosaurine nested between Brontosaurus excelsus and Brontosaurus yahnahpin.

facts.statement: Researchers classified Amphicoelias as the basalmost diplodocid outside Apatosaurinae and Diplodocinae due to its primitive features and mixed morphology.
facts.quote: The authors instead opted to classify Amphicoelias as the basalmost diplodocid outside Apatosaurinae and Diplodocinae, having primitive features, minimal significant differences from either subfamily, a slightly more parsimonious apatosaurine phylogeny, but a slightly more diplodocine morphology.

facts.statement: In 2025, Mannion and Moore confirmed that various phylogenetic placements of Amphicoelias within the clade are considered parsimonious.
facts.quote: In 2025, Mannion and Moore also recovered similar results in their phylogenetic analyses, with various placements of Amphicoelias within the clade all being considered parsimonious.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that benefits like predator immunity and longer lifespans were secondary advantages of the giant size of Amphicoelias.
facts.quote: Carpenter argued that other benefits of large size, such as relative immunity from predators, lower energy expenditure, and longer life span, are probably secondary advantages.

facts.statement: Amphicoelias lived in a savanna-like environment where poor-quality food likely drove the evolution of its giant size.
facts.quote: The environment of Amphicoelias was essentially a savanna, similar to the arid environments in which modern giant herbivores are found, supporting the idea that poor-quality food in an arid environment promotes the evolution of giant herbivores.

facts.statement: Carpenter speculated that Amphicoelias may have used gallery forests for shade during the day and fed on the savanna at night.
facts.quote: Carpenter speculated that giant herbivores like Amphicoelias may have used the shade of the gallery forests to stay cool during the day, and done most of their feeding on the open savanna at night.

facts.statement: Amphicoelias altus was approximately 25 meters long, similar in size to Diplodocus.
facts.quote: A. altus era también similar en tamaño al Diplodocus, de alrededor de 25 metros de largo.

facts.statement: Edward Drinker Cope named Amphicoelias altus in December 1877 (published 1878) based on an incomplete skeleton containing two vertebrae, a pubis, the pelvis, and a femur.
facts.quote: Amphicoelias altus, fue nombrada por el paleontólogo Edward Drinker Cope en diciembre de 1877, aunque no se publicó hasta 1878, por un esqueleto incompleto que consta de dos vértebras, un pubis, la cadera, y un fémur, hueso de la parte superior de la pierna.

facts.statement: Amphicoelias had homodont dentition with long, thin cylindrical teeth spaced out and projecting forward.
facts.quote: La dentición de Amphicoelias es homodonta. Sus dientes tienen forma de varillas cilíndricas largas y delgadas, están espaciados y se proyectan hacia el frente de la boca.

facts.statement: The femur of Amphicoelias is unusually long, thin, and round in cross-section.
facts.quote: El fémur de Amphicoelias es inusualmente largo, delgado y redondo en sección transversal.

facts.statement: While most scientists distinguish Amphicoelias and Diplodocus as separate genera, at least one researcher suggests Amphicoelias is likely the older synonym of Diplodocus.
facts.quote: Aunque la mayoría de los científicos han utilizado estos datos para distinguir Amphicoelias y Diplodocus como géneros separados, por lo menos uno ha sugerido que Amphicoelias es probablemente el sinónimo más antiguo de Diplodocus.

facts.statement: Even in 1881, it was recognized that A. altus could not be distinguished from other genera because Cope's described characteristics were misinterpreted and widespread.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, incluso en 1881, se reconoció que A. altus no se pudo distinguir de otros géneros, ya que las características descritas por Cope fueron mal interpretadas y están muy extendidas.

facts.statement: Amphicoelias altus lived during the Late Jurassic, approximately 150 to 145 million years ago (Kimmeridgian and Tithonian stages), in what is now North America.
facts.quote: Amphicoelias altus (del gr. "carácter hueco en ambos lados alto") es la única especie conocida del género extinto Amphicoelias de dinosaurio saurópodo diplodócido, que vivió a finales del Jurásico, hace aproximadamente 150 y 145 millones de años, en el Kimmeridgiense y el Titoniense, en lo que hoy es Norteamérica.

facts.statement: Amphicoelias fossils are found in stratigraphic zone 6 of the Morrison Formation.
facts.quote: Amphicoelias está presente en la zona estratigráfica 6 de la Formación Morrison.

facts.statement: The genus Amphicoelias was established by Cope in 1877.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Cope, 1877

facts.statement: The species Amphicoelias altus was described by Cope in 1877.
facts.quote: species_authority: Cope, 1877

facts.statement: Amphicoelias is classified in the family Diplodocidae.
facts.quote: familia: Diplodocidae

facts.statement: Amphicoelias belongs to the subfamily Apatosaurinae.
facts.quote: subfamilia: Apatosaurinae

facts.statement: Amphicoelias is the genus name for this extinct dinosaur.
facts.quote: genus: Amphicoelias

facts.statement: A. altus is the only known species within the genus Amphicoelias.
facts.quote: species: A. altus

facts.statement: Amphicoelias is classified within the suborder Sauropodomorpha.
facts.quote: subordo: Sauropodomorpha

facts.statement: Amphicoelias belongs to the infraorder Sauropoda.
facts.quote: infraordo: Sauropoda

facts.statement: Amphicoelias is part of the order Saurischia.
facts.quote: ordo: Saurischia

facts.statement: Amphicoelias is classified in the superorder Dinosauria.
facts.quote: superordo: Dinosauria

facts.statement: Amphicoelias belongs to the phylum Chordata.
facts.quote: phylum: Chordata

facts.statement: Amphicoelias is classified in the kingdom Animalia.
facts.quote: regnum: Animalia

facts.statement: Studies of giant mammalian herbivores like elephants and rhinos suggest that larger size improves food digestion efficiency in plant-eating animals.
facts.quote: Carpenter cited several studies of giant mammalian herbivores, such as elephants and rhinoceros, which showed that larger size in plant-eating animals leads to greater efficiency in digesting food.

facts.statement: Sauropod dinosaurs throughout their history lived primarily in semi-arid, seasonally dry environments with seasonal drops in food quality.
facts.quote: Throughout their evolutionary history, sauropod dinosaurs were found primarily in semi-arid, seasonally dry environments, with a corresponding seasonal drop in the quality of food during the dry season.

facts.statement: Carpenter argued that the sauropod digestive system's adaptation to low-quality food allowed ferns to be a major part of their diet.
facts.quote: Carpenter argued that the sauropod digestive system, well adapted to handle low-quality food, allows for the consumption of ferns as a large part of the sauropod diet.

facts.statement: Edward Drinker Cope described the genus Amphicoelias in two issues of the American Naturalist in 1878.
facts.quote: Edward Drinker Cope describió sus hallazgos en dos números de 1878 del American Naturalist y los asignó al nuevo género Amphicoelias.

facts.statement: The first species named in the genus, Amphicoelias altus, was discovered by Cope in 1877.
facts.quote: Las primeras especies nombradas en el género, Amphicoelias altus, holotipo AMHD 5764, fue descubierto por Cope en 1877.

facts.statement: Cope named a second species, Amphicoelias latus, in 1878.
facts.quote: Cope también nombró una segunda especie en 1878, Amphicoelias latus.

facts.statement: Based on an illustration published in 1878, the vertebra of A. fragillimus was estimated to be 2.7 meters tall in life.
facts.quote: Basada únicamente en una ilustración publicada en 1878, esta vértebra habría medido 2,7 metros de altura en vida.

facts.statement: It has been argued that a typographical error in the published scale bar meant the fossil vertebra was actually only 1.38 meters tall.
facts.quote: Se ha argumentado que la barra de escala en la descripción publicada contenía un error tipográfico, y la vértebra fósil en realidad tenía solo 1,38 metros de altura.

facts.statement: In 2018, A. fragillimus was assigned its own genus, Maraapunisaurus.
facts.quote: En 2018, "A." fragillimus recibió su propio género, Maraapunisaurus.

facts.statement: Lucas discovered a partial vertebra of the new species in Colorado, near the mine where Camarasaurus was found.
facts.quote: Lucas descubrió una vértebra parcial (el arco neural y la espina dorsal) de la nueva especie en Colorado, cerca de la mina en que se descubrió Camarasaurus.

facts.statement: Cope estimated the vertebra to be up to 2.4 meters tall in its complete form, while Ken Carpenter estimated it at 2.7 meters.
facts.quote: Cope lo estimó en hasta 2,4 metros de alto en su forma completa, mientras que Ken Carpenter en 2,7 metros.

facts.statement: The presence of dinosaurs like Camarasaurus in the same rocks suggests the site belongs to the Morrison Formation, dating it to 150 million years ago in the late Jurassic period, specifically the Tithonian.
facts.quote: la presencia de dinosaurios tales como Camarasaurus en las mismas rocas indica que pertenecen probablemente a la formación de Morrison, lo que pone la edad del sitio en 150 millones de años, en lo último del período Jurásico, específicamente en el Titoniense.

facts.statement: Carpenter disagreed with the synonymy of A. altus and A. fragillimus in 2006, citing numerous differences in vertebra construction observed by Cope, and suggested these differences justify a separate species or even genus for A. fragillimus.
facts.quote: Carpenter en 2006 no estuvo de acuerdo con la sinonimia de A. altus y A. fragillimus, sin embargo, citó numerosas diferencias en la construcción de la vértebra también observada por Cope, y sugirió que estas diferencias son suficientes para justificar una especie separada o incluso un género separado para A. fragillimus.

facts.statement: The discovery of Amphicoelias occurred during the famous Bone Wars, when paleontologists Othniel Charles Marsh and Edward Drinker Cope competed to find the most fossils and new species.
facts.quote: Fue un período famoso en la historia de la paleontología, cuando se enfrentaron dos paleontólogos preeminentes, Othniel Charles Marsh y Edward Drinker Cope, quienes competían por quién podría encontrar la mayor cantidad de fósiles y especies nuevas.

facts.statement: While rumors of fraud or exaggeration existed, the circumstances surrounding Maraapunisaurus fragillimus raised doubts about the authenticity of the find.
facts.quote: Mientras existieron rumores de un fraude o exageración, las circunstancias que rodearon a Maraapunisaurus fragillimus levantaron dudas sobre la autenticidad del hallazgo.

facts.statement: Cope placed it in a unique family, Amphicoeliidae, which is now considered a nomen oblitum (forgotten name).
facts.quote: Lo colocó en una familia única, Amphicoeliidae , aunque ahora se considera un nomen oblitum, nombre olvidado.

facts.statement: A. altus is known from better remains than other species.
facts.quote: A. altus se conoce de mejores restos.

facts.statement: Although A. latus is clearly not Amphicoelias, it is likely a synonym of Camarasaurus grandis rather than C. supremus because it was found lower in the Morrison Formation and its deeply concave caudal vertebral articular faces are more consistent with C. grandis.
facts.quote: Aunque Amphicoelias latus claramente no es Amphicoelias , probablemente sea sinónimo de Camarasaurus grandis en lugar de C. supremus porque se encontró más abajo en la Formación Morrison y las caras articulares profundamente cóncavas en las vértebras caudales son más consistentes con C. grandis.

facts.statement: A cladogram shows the relationships of A. altus with other diplodocids based on the analysis by Tschopp and Mateus in 2017.
facts.quote: El cladograma a continuación muestra las relaciones de A. altus con otros diplodócidos, según lo encontrado por el análisis de Tschopp y Mateus de 2017.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that large size in herbivores increases digestive efficiency, citing modern elephants and rhinoceroses as examples.
facts.quote: Carpenter cita varios estudios de mamíferos herbívoros gigantes, tales como el elefante y el rinoceronte, donde se demostró que un tamaño más grande en animales herbívoros conduce a mayor eficacia en la digestión del alimento.

facts.statement: Large animals have longer digestive systems that retain food for longer periods, allowing them to survive on low-quality food sources.
facts.quote: Puesto que los animales más grandes tienen sistemas digestivos más largos, el alimento se mantiene en el proceso digestivo por períodos de tiempo perceptiblemente más largos, permitiendo que los animales grandes sobrevivan con fuentes de baja calidad alimenticia.

facts.statement: Sauropod dinosaurs were mostly found in semi-arid environments with seasonal dry periods, leading to lower food quality during the dry season.
facts.quote: A través de su historia evolutiva, los dinosaurios saurópodos fueron encontrados sobre todo en ambientes semiáridos, estacionales secos y con lluvia estacional, con una correspondiente disminución en la calidad del alimento durante la estación seca.

facts.statement: Amphicoelias lived in an essentially savanna environment, supporting the idea that poor-quality food in arid settings promotes the evolution of giant herbivores.
facts.quote: El ambiente del amficoelias era esencialmente una sabana, similar a los ambientes áridos en los cuales se encuentran los herbívoros gigantes modernos, apoyando la idea que el alimento de mala calidad en un ambiente árido promueve la evolución de herbívoros gigantes.

facts.statement: Carpenter suggested that predator immunity, lower energy costs, and longer life are likely secondary advantages of large size.
facts.quote: Carpenter sugirió que otras ventajas del tamaño grande, tales como la inmunidad relativa a los depredadores, gastos energéticos más bajos y una vida más larga son probablemente ventajas secundarias.

facts.statement: Although the Morrison Formation environment resembled a modern savanna, ferns were likely the dominant plants and main food source for Amphicoelias since grass did not appear until the end of the Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Decíamos que el ambiente de la formación de Morrison en el cual Amphicoelias vivió se habría parecido a una sabana moderna, aunque, puesto que la hierba no apareció hasta el final del Cretáceo, los helechos eran probablemente las plantas dominantes y las fuentes principales del alimento para el amficoelias.

facts.statement: Engelmann et al. mention that ferns were not a food source for sauropods due to their relatively low caloric content.
facts.quote: Engelmann et al. mencionan que los helechos no fueron la fuente de alimento para los saurópodos debido a su contenido calórico relativamente bajo.

facts.statement: Carpenter proposes that sauropod digestive systems adapted to handle low-quality food, allowing them to digest ferns as a major part of their diet.
facts.quote: Carpenter propone que el sistema digestivo de los saurópodos se adaptó para manejar el alimento de baja calidad, permitiendo la digestión de helechos como gran parte de su dieta.

facts.statement: Carpenter observed that occasional large fossil trunks indicate the presence of trees 20-30 meters tall, which seems to conflict with comparisons of the environment to a modern savanna.
facts.quote: Carpenter también observó que la presencia ocasional de grandes troncos fósiles indica la presencia de árboles de 20-30 m de alto, lo que parecería estar en conflicto con la comparación del ambiente con la sabana actual.

facts.statement: Trees were likely rare and existed in gallery forests along rivers and water accumulation sites because tall trees require more water than the savanna environment could provide.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, los árboles son raros, y puesto que los altos requieren más agua de la que el ambiente de la sabana podría proporcionar, estos existieron probablemente en bosques de galería a lo largo de los ríos y en los sitios en donde el agua se podía acumular.

facts.statement: Carpenter speculated that giant herbivores like Amphicoelias may have used forest cover to stay cool during the day and fed in open savannas at night.
facts.quote: Carpenter especuló que los herbívoros gigantes como el amficoelias pudieron haber utilizado la cortina de los bosques para permanecer frescos durante el día, y haber hecho la mayor parte de su alimentación en la sabana abierta por la noche.

facts.statement: Amphicoelias belongs to the parent group Diplodocoidea.
facts.quote: Parent group: Diplodocoidea

facts.statement: Amphicoelias is classified in the class Saurischia.
facts.quote: Class: Saurischia

facts.quote: Fossil occurrences recorded: 3
